YesNCSC objected. This is not how hybrid is done.ORANGE supported this. It was asked to minute the detailed reasons for objection from NCSC: "PQ/T hybrid schemes built from NIST 203 should use approved key combiners in the sense of SP 800-277. We have a number to choose from which meet all the security requirements for hybrid schemes. Deviating from standardised approved cryptographic norms to devise our own scheme is not necessary and introduces risk which needs evaluation. In general 'roll-your-own' is not good practice. Since alternatives exist, and profile slots are limited, we do not think it is appropriate to pursue the solution proposed in '277. I also checked the study - nested hybrids were not identified to be taken forward to normative work. "
